title: Subscriber persona matrix and micro-schedules (draft)
body:
Purpose:
Draft working notes for a lightweight persona-driven approach to channel selection + micro-scheduling for the Alerts & Notifications console. Focus is: when to ring whom, what channel to prefer, and how to let tenants express minimal rules without combinatorial explosion.

Status: quick brainstorm -> grooming doc. Not final. Wants product + SRE input before moving to a proto wireframe.

Context / problem statements (why this exists):
- Teams want predictable oncall noise while maintaining SLO visibility for business owners.
- Current console forces users to pick channels per alert and set global thresholds; this gets noisy at scale and is brittle across teams with overlapping ownerships.
- We need common heuristics that cover 80% of use cases without requiring per-alert complex policy trees.

Design goals (constraints):
- Minimal config: 3–4 persona profiles to pick from, plus one advanced policy option.
- Deterministic tie-breakers: channel preference order, escalation delay, and fallback policy.
- Respect business hours and micro-schedules (15m slots) for low-friction quieting rules.
- Support multi-tenant defaults (org-level, team-level, route-level).

Proposed building blocks:
1) Subscriber persona (primary selector) — single-choice per subscriber or default:
   - Primary Responder: immediate, push + call if no ack within timeout. (SRE oncall, pager)
   - Secondary/Stakeholder: delayed, email + slack thread mention after 10m. (product manager)
   - Observer: digest, daily summary or monthly SLA report. (execs, infra leads)
   - Do Not Disturb (DND): only critical routed incidents, otherwise suppressed. (follow-the-sun roles)

2) Channel affinity & ordering (per persona):
   - Push -> SMS -> Phone -> Slack DM -> Email -> Digest
   - Allow tenant to re-order channels at org-level.

3) Micro-schedules (fine-grained quiet windows):
   - 15-minute blocks that can be chained into business-hours presets.
   - Presets: 24/7, 9–5 weekdays, follow-the-sun, custom rotations.
   - Persona-aware quieting: e.g., Stakeholder persona auto-snoozes push between 22:00–07:00 local time (configurable).

4) Escalation rules (simple, predictable):
   - Base rule: notify primary immediately, wait X minutes (default 5) -> notify secondary, wait Y minutes -> call primary escalation.
   - Make X and Y tenant-configurable but expose sane defaults per persona.

5) Noise-reduction heuristics (auto-suggestions):
   - If a route generates > N alerts in M minutes, suggest throttling (suppress repeated notifications for identical fingerprint for T minutes).
   - Suggest combining related low-severity alerts into a single digest if same resource and same minute window.

Wireframe notes (quick sketches to support in-console flows):
- Persona selector appears on the subscriber modal: dropdown with short description and "preview channels" row.
- At team level, a compact grid of personas with toggles to set team defaults and an "apply to existing routes" bulk action.
- Micro-schedule editor: timeline bar (24h) with drag-to-create blocks; each persona row has its own bar.
- Escalation timeline visualizer: single horizontal timeline showing who gets pinged at t=0, t=5, t=15 with icons and contact channel badges.
- Conflict hinting: if org default conflicts with route override, show warning pill with quick action: keep org / use route / merge.

Open questions / tradeoffs: 
- How many personas are too many? We want to avoid creating a taxonomy that looks like an org chart. Start with 3–4.
- Should micro-schedules be per-person or per-persona? Per-persona is simpler; per-person could be used by advanced users.
- Timezones: should schedules be tenant-local, subscriber-local, or resource-local? Default to subscriber-local but allow org override.
- Integration with on-call & external pagers (PagerDuty): map personas to external escalation policies vs native console. Keep mapping simple: persona -> external policy id string.

Edge cases to handle: 
- Subscribers with multiple contacts (email + phone): need clear ordering + fallback on contact method failure.
- Users who prefer only SMS/Phone for safety-critical alerts — expose a 'safety' toggle that forces voice calls for critical severities.
- Overlapping rotations: team A and team B both own a route; need merge rules for combined subscriber lists and escalation paths.

Acceptance criteria for an initial beta:
- Org default persona + one team override path is editable in the console.
- Persona selection in subscriber modal showing channel preview.
- Micro-schedule UI supports creating presets and applying to persona.
- Escalation visualizer matches backend timeline config and shows simulated pings.
- Throttling suggestion triggers in the UI for noisy routes.

Implementation notes / backend hints (for infra & serving-runtime team review):
- Backend should expose a compact policy descriptor (persona_id, channel_order[], schedule_id, escalation_offsets[]). Keep schema small for rn.
- Policy evaluation should be deterministic and fast: evaluate persona -> local schedule -> channel order -> escalation offsets -> send pipeline.
- Caching: cache subscriber lookups and schedule expansions for 5 minutes to reduce decision latency.
- Compatibility: ensure fallback to existing per-route channel config when tenant not using personas.

Next steps / grooming checklist:
- [ ] Walk this doc with SRE and Solutions Eng (assign: Ravi) by 2025-02-05.
- [ ] Prototype persona modal + schedule timeline in Figma (assign: Clara) by 2025-02-14.
- [ ] Backend schema draft and perf targets (assign: Jonas) by 2025-02-21.
- [ ] UX test 5 quick flows with 3 internal teams and capture failure modes (owner: Ava) by 2025-03-07.

Notes to self: keep the initial mental model simple. Personas are a UX abstraction not a full RBAC replacement.

Slack refs / tickets: see linked artifacts above.

Unresolved: do we allow per-alert manual "mute for 30m" from the incident page? probably yes — separate quick-snooze API needed.

End of draft.
